proof:
# Unequal endpoint coupling with an explicit density ceiling

Let A,B be full-dimensional convex bodies in R^d, d>=1, with
0<a=|A|<=b=|B|. Suppose K is a convex body containing (A+B)/2,
and write k=|K|. Define

    v_*=((a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))/2)^d.

There is one actual measure eta supported in (A+B)/2 satisfying

    eta(R^d)=a,
    eta<=(a/v_*) dx,
    centroid(eta)=(g_A+g_B)/2.                          (1)

For every u and every pair of real thresholds beta+tau,beta-tau,

    eta{u.x>=beta}
      <=|A intersect{u.x>=beta+tau}|
         +(a/b)|B intersect{u.x>=beta-tau}|.            (2)

The same eta works for all thresholds and directions. In particular it
is dominated by ordinary volume on K, since a<=v_*. This is not a
replacement of the larger endpoint by a smaller body.

## 1. Exact density calculation for the full endpoint bodies

Use the actual triangular conditional-quantile map T from the direct
conditional-Fubini coupling proof, now transporting uniform probability
on A to uniform probability on B. All of its continuity, conditional
positivity, endpoint, and repeated-substitution arguments are unchanged.
Its positive own-coordinate derivatives t_i now telescope to

    product_i t_i=b/a.

The midpoint map Z=(I+T)/2 is still triangular and injective. Its
conditional Jacobian product satisfies the sharper bound

    J_Z=2^(-d)product_i(1+t_i)
        >=[(1+(b/a)^(1/d))/2]^d=v_*/a.                 (3)

For completeness, expand product(1+t_i) by subset size j. The product
of all products indexed by j-element subsets equals
(product_i t_i)^(binomial(d-1,j-1)). Their geometric mean is therefore
(product_i t_i)^(j/d). Arithmetic-geometric mean bounds their sum
below by binomial(d,j) times that value. Summing in j gives(3);
j=0 and j=d are exact and cause no undefined exponent.

The conditional substitution formula consequently gives midpoint-law
density at most 1/v_*. Set eta=a Law(Z(X)) for X uniform on A.
Then(1) follows from that density bound and linearity of first moments.
The associated coupling's first marginal is ordinary volume on A and
its second marginal is (a/b) times ordinary volume on B. The pointwise
closed-halfspace midpoint implication proves(2), including all boundary
equalities. These are actual full endpoint marginals; neither g_B nor
the support of B is replaced by that of a chosen subset.

## 2. One valid middle source and its all-cap bounds

Put A,K,B at integer bases -1,0,1. The convex hull has exactly these
fibers. Define

    y=[k g_K+a(g_A+g_B)]/(k+2a),       Y=(0,y).           (4)

The point y is the centroid of 1_K dx+2eta. It belongs to K, since
the measure is supported in K; hence Y is an actual mixed point.
Except when a=b, this is not asserted to be the true mixed centroid.

For every nonvertical ambient halfspace through Y, (2) and a/b<=1
make its actual endpoint cap sum at least eta(H_0), where H_0 is the
corresponding through-y halfspace in the middle fiber. The all-dimensional
mass-dependent dominated-centroid theorem therefore gives

    D_S(Y)>(3/4)Gamma_d(k+a).                           (5)

Its uniform positive surplus justifies the strict depth infimum. Pure
integer halfspaces contain K and at least the smaller endpoint, of
mass k+a, and have their own positive surplus. Parallel inward
translation covers halfspaces containing but not passing through Y.

Thus the desired n=1 OC bound follows at Y whenever k+a>=2b.
This condition is sufficient only; no assertion is made about its
complementary unequal-volume regime.

In the plane the stronger density theorem gives the additional bound

    D_S(Y)>=c_*(k+2a),       c_*=6144/22745.              (6)

It uses eta<=1_K, retaining the stronger actual ceiling a/v_* as
additional available data. There is no implicit substitution of the
smaller subsystem mass for the original mixed total k+a+b.

## 3. A complete planar endpoint-ratio window

For d=2, suppose a<=b<=5a/3. Then the single point(4) satisfies

    D_S(Y)>(2/9)(k+a+b),                               (7)

for every compatible K, without a restriction on its area beyond
actual convex compatibility.

Indeed (3), or ordinary Brunn--Minkowski, gives

    k>=v_*=(a+b+2sqrt(ab))/4>=(b+3a)/4.

Since c_*>2/9, subtracting the right side of(7) from(6) and inserting
this lower bound for k yields

    c_*(k+2a)-(2/9)(k+a+b)
       >=(c_*/4-5/18)b+(11c_*/4-7/18)a.

The coefficient of b is negative. Using b<=5a/3, the last expression
is at least

    [(19/6)c_*-23/27]a=(2177/614115)a>0.               (8)

This is a uniform original-mass surplus, valid for every ambient
direction and every cut status. The endpoint-ratio statement itself
could alternatively be deduced by shrinking B about its own centroid
to area a and invoking the equal-volume coupled bound. Such a deduction
does not supply the stronger density ceiling(1). This note keeps those
two conclusions distinct: (1) is a full-body unequal transport
invariant; (7) is one proved numerical consequence, not a resolution
for arbitrary endpoint imbalance.

## 4. Exact payment from the stronger density ceiling

The ceiling in(1) provides a further all-dimensional improvement at the
same actual source(4). Put

    theta=a/v_* in(0,1],
    A_d=1/Gamma_d,
    epsilon_d=d Delta_d/(d+1)>0,

where Delta_d is the explicitly proved positive dual margin in the
all-dimensional mass-dependent centroid source. Then

    D_S(Y)>=(3/4)Gamma_d(k+a)
      +(3/4)Gamma_d^2 k
         [(1-theta)/(3Gamma_d)+theta epsilon_d]
             /(1+2a/k)^d.                             (9)

This is a concrete density-dependent mass bound, not a claim that it
always pays the full asymmetric OC target.

Here is a complete derivation of the additional term. Rescale the
actual coupling measure to eta'=eta/theta<=1_K dx. Its mass is v_*,
and the law whose centroid is y remains exactly

    1_K dx+2theta eta'.

After normalizing |K|=1, set alpha=eta'(K), s=|K intersect H|,
r=eta'(H), U=1/s, E=r/s, Q=(s+alpha-r)/s. Repeating the actual
cap-root Jensen and two-interval bathtub argument with coefficient
2theta in place of two gives

    phi(U)+2theta phi(Q)+2theta phi(E)>=2theta/(d+1),
    phi(t)=t-[d/(d+1)]t^(1+1/d).                       (10)

No arbitrary new law or changed source is introduced. The actual
captured budget is s+theta r by(2). Set L=4A_d/3-1 and

    D_theta=U+theta Q-theta L E.

The same Fenchel multipliers as in the all-dimensional proof yield

    D_theta<=A_d+theta X_d,
    X_d=[2d/(d+1)] [(1+1/(2d))^(d+1)
                       +(1-L/(2d))_+^(d+1)-1]
       =1+A_d/3-epsilon_d.

Equivalently,

    D_theta<=theta+4A_d/3
                    -[(1-theta)A_d/3+theta epsilon_d].

The exact identity (1+theta alpha)/s=U+theta Q+theta E-theta
therefore gives

    s+theta r >=(3/(4A_d))
       [1+theta alpha+((1-theta)A_d/3+theta epsilon_d)s]. (11)

Initial Jensen alone bounds
s>=Gamma_d/(1+2theta alpha)^d. Undoing normalization,
theta alpha=a/k, so(11) becomes precisely(9).

Pure integer directions also satisfy(9). Indeed epsilon_d<=A_d/3:
the binomial theorem gives
(1+1/(2d))^(d+1)>=1+(d+1)/(2d), whence X_d>=1.
Thus the right side of(9) is at most
Gamma_d k+(3/4)Gamma_d a<k+a, the mass retained by either pure
integer through-middle halfspace. Containing halfspaces reduce to
through-source halfspaces as before.

For fixed b,k and a decreasing to zero, the right side of(9) tends
to Gamma_d k, recovering the ordinary middle-centroid budget. The
coarser first term alone would instead tend to(3/4)Gamma_d k.
This identifies exactly how the unequal transport ceiling enters this
dual. The archived fixed-mass Jensen estimates also recover the ordinary
small-mass limit; no superiority to every such estimate is claimed.
No claim is made that this limit argument moves a
selected center in a proof of the full conjecture; (9) is a direct
finite-parameter inequality at the explicitly defined source.
